key_insight: An explainable deep reinforcement learning framework can optimize residential building energy management while making battery-control decisions more transparent and trustworthy.
engineering_relevance: For building energy systems with PV, storage, dynamic tariffs, and weather uncertainty, this approach offers a practical control strategy that can reduce costs and support real-world deployment.
method: Trains on-policy and off-policy DRL agents for building energy control
Uses an expanded state space with demand, PV output, battery state, prices, weather, calendar, and forecasts
Applies post-hoc explainability methods to interpret learned policies
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on both synthetic data and real-world Living Lab Energy Campus data, and A2C and PPO achieved the best cumulative rewards and policy stability among the tested agents.
watch_item: Because the policy depends on many real-time signals and forecasts, performance may degrade when sensor quality, forecast accuracy, or system dynamics change.
paper_title: Explainable Data-driven Deep Reinforcement Learning Methods for Optimal Energy Management in Buildings
